newsitem.title: CHINA: China property market to rebound in 1997 - newspaper.
newsitem.headline: China property market to rebound in 1997 - newspaper.

text.p: China's property market is expected to rebound in 1997 after a slump over the past couple of years with housing prices in key cities already moving up, the China Daily Business Weekly said on Sunday.
The newspaper said housing prices in 16 cities surveyed rose slightly in the fourth quarter of 1996, indicating a rebound was on the horizon thanks to an improving national economy and low inflation.
Industry analysts said recent moves to reduce the myriad local taxes imposed on property projects should also help improve the market.
Virtually all Chinese in urban areas lived in housing allocated to them by their work units up to the mid-1980s, when the government began an experiment with commercial housing.
There was a boom in self-bought housing in the late 1980s and early 1990s, followed by a slump due to over-construction and prices rising well beyond the means of ordinary workers.
In Shanghai, a two-bedroom apartment on the outskirts of the city can cost 350,000 yuan compared with an average annual income of around 7,000 yuan for a worker.

China has a huge urban housing imbalance with empty housing stock estimated at more than 40 million square metres, while per capita living space for Chinese urban dwellers is only 7.7 square metres, the Shanghai Securities News said on Sunday.
China's retail price inflation was a year-on-year 6.1 percent in 1996, down sharply from a year-on-year 14.8 percent for 1995, officials figures show.
